utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. I am not sure whether we have tendered the exhibits from the last witness. In any event --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we did not yet. Yes, I agree with you. Since we changed Registrars again, I will ask the present Registrar whether she is in a position to guide us, if not, we will do it after the first break. Madam Registrar, has the... If you would prefer to have some more time, we will do it after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would prefer to deal with it after the first break, Mr. Ierace, since there has been a change of Registrars, as you might have noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. One other -- a few other outstanding matters very quickly. In relation to DP5, I could indicate very quickly the shortcomings in relation to rule 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be of any use to write them down. As far as the Chamber is concerned, and also a consolidated list, so that we have not the same problem as we have with summaries, that you have to grab small parts and pieces from everywhere. But perhaps it is good that you mention them very briefly, and then perhaps put them in a consolidated document that I hope will not be too long, but finally that we have all your 65 ter complaints together. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, would you wish that I do that orally or just in writing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would just do it very briefly orally and then we will later see it on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to DP5, we were not informed of the company to which the witness belonged or the battalion or that the company included a tank or where he was headquartered for the relevant periods, or that he would give evidence as to the obtaining of weapons from the JNA barracks, police buildings, and state companies. All that he will give evidence of the objective of mortar firing by the ABiH in relation to sniper incident 23. We were not forewarned that he would give evidence that there were no buildings or even remains of buildings on the Bosnian-Serb Army side of the relevant part of the confrontation lines or that there was an artillery position near where the victim was shot or that he would give evidence of places on the ABiH side where ammunitions were manufactured or in relation to the digging of trenches on the ABiH side by persons of Serbian ethnicity. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since Mr. Ierace did not wish to express himself in writing -- no, Mr. President, since Mr. Ierace is wasting time, I am not going to waste time. Everything is in a letter of 29th of October, 2002. We spoke about the weapons. We spoke about other weapons in possession of the ABiH Army. We spoke of the proximity and the confusion of buildings. We spoke about contradictory character of certain documents. We spoke of many things that resulted in the letter 29th of October, 2002. It seems a little strange that we are told that we had never informed them. Now, if every time we have to give a statement within -- have to give a statement extensive, then we can stop hearing the witnesses and we can just work by email. I don't think that is normal that the Prosecution is complaining every single day, every single day they are complaining, while the Defence is doing everything it can to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I allowed the Prosecution, briefly to indicate orally the points they said they missed. You have pointed to the sources where the Prosecution, in your view, might have found it. For this very moment, is that enough to deal with the issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, as I foreshadowed, I indicate that the most recent update to the 65 ter in relation to the next witness is letter dated the 6th of November, 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's your starting point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can now deal with the exhibits. Perhaps do it now rather than after the break. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1784, under seal, pseudonym sheet; Exhibit D1785, map; Exhibit D348I, video; Exhibit P3759, photograph; Exhibit P3761, photograph marked by witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have objections that you know already in relation to these two photographs. We still have the same position. We cannot take something by the means that we have already told you about, so you know our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You also know that the Chamber has ruled on it, so that objection was already denied. Then D1784 is admitted under seal. The other documents and videotape are admitted into evidence. Mr. Usher, could you then please escort the witness into the courtroom. Yes -- the protective measures has been granted as requested; that means pseudonym and facial distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, whilst the witness is being brought in, we were informed yesterday of a new exhibit in relation to this witness which is a simply a reference to the various sniping maps. Perhaps we could be informed which particular sniping map the Prosecution now seeks to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence said that this was map 3274, but I informed the case manager, the Prosecution, that by this witness we will not introduce any evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No document, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language -- may I ask you to stand up again. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving testimony in this court, Witness, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration is handed out to you now by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first page will just do. That's the other languages. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Protective measures have been granted in respect of you. That means that no one outside of this courtroom can see your face, and that we will call you by a pseudonym. You will first be examined by counsel for the Defence. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, considering that the Trial Chamber has approved protective measures for you, the Defence would like you to have a look at a document that you see before you. Is the data correct that's in this document, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Considering that the protective measures have been approved for you, as I have already told you, we will address you as DP21.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since we wish to get some biographical data in respect of Witness DP21, the Defence would ask for a closed session so that the witness can give us some other biographical data in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, when you told us where you were born and where you lived in 1992, could you tell us in relation to the centre of town what is the part of the town in terms of the north, south, west, east?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: It is the eastern part. It is going in the easterly direction from the Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP21, we will be speaking about the period from September 1992 until August of 1994. Where were you in September 1992, although I wish to stress that you do not have to say the name of the village where you were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: I was in my village. I can say it, but I didn't go anywhere. In 1992 in September, I was in my own village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992 in your village, were there some incidents that occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Not in the village itself, but we did have some problems because we lived next to Muslims, our neighbours were Muslims, and we had some fear and discomfort because at the time we were afraid of some misfortune occurring like in 1942 when villages were burned and children and civilians killed and their throats cut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. But let us focus on the time of 1992. When I asked you if we -- if there were some incidents that occurred in your village, and you said that you were in fear. You, as a citizen, and others citizens of your village, did you take any steps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: We took some steps, in fact, in April, even. So that was well before September, in the local commune of Hresa consisting of five villages. In the evening, one evening, we met, we had a discussion to see what we can do because Serbs started leaving the downtown. They were leaving with bags, with luggage, and what happened already, suffering for the Orthodox people, that is for the Serb started. There was the Patriotic League that was starting to be active, and wherever Serbs went, were --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, could you please speak slowly and give me short answers. So, what you are saying is that in April 1992 in your village, you were -- you organised yourselves at the local commune?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us very briefly what were the steps that you took, specifically.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Specifically, I can say that we created a defence for the villages, guard posts, where we stood guard to defend our villages so that they wouldn't be burnt down again, as it happened in 1942.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, when you say "our villages," you said that this is easterly direction in relation to Sarajevo. How many villages covered your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: These were five villages in the local commune of Hresa. And in these villages lived Orthodox peoples, and that's how we decided to protect our villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that we can understand the situation very clearly, considering that you lived in that part of Sarajevo, could you tell us if in the vicinity of the villages where you lived, were there also villages populated exclusively by Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes. There were villages, for instance, Vasan Han there were also Serb houses there also Muslim houses. And there was a threat for us from the city of Sarajevo because the Muslim started preparing certain bad things, so we had to be prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, in September 1992, could you tell us how were you organised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, in September 1992, this was our initiative, that's how we were organised without any other participation because we didn't have any leaders. We organised ourselves for our villages. These were like village guards, village patrols. We created a position, a line in front of the village, to protect the people inside so we would be there on the meadows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you established a line or a position, and that you were on meadows in front of your houses, could you tell us: Did you have any kind of protection on these lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Not to start with, but later on when our lines started to be shelled and attacks were launched, then we started to fortify our positions to dig ourselves in, to create trenches, because we were also threatened by daily sniping from the Muslims because you could just be hit. So we had to dig ourselves in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP21, now that you have answered this Defence question, can you tell us in relation to your lines, that is, in that easterly part of Sarajevo you told us which villages these were. Were there positions in the proximity of your line, were there lines that were established by other entities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, in front of us, ahead of us, there was a Muslim line which Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was perhaps 150 metres away from us as the crow flies in that part, and they were on one side and we were on the other side. That is, we were on the eastern side and they were towards the west they were facing -- they would turn towards the west in respect of our line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, with respect to your line, can you tell us what weapons did you have, can you tell us that first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: You mean our line, my line?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: To start with, we didn't have any weapons. Some people would have a hunting rifle, that's true. Then somebody would just come along to stand guard. People had what they were able to get their hands on, so that's how we managed to protect ourselves, just to be there to stop them while the population would be able to leave, so just to avoid them being killed again. That is what the -- that was the agreement, that was what we agreed to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on, you said you didn't start with any weapons or get any weapons. Did you get better weapons later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, we did get better weapons later. When we got to it line, we realised we were under risk, we realised we were under threat and we had to arm ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how did you do that? How did you get more weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, we were fortunate, although it is perhaps not a good word to use, but there were some warehouses in Faletici where the army had been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that there was a warehouse of the Territorial Defence in Faletici where the army had been, do you have any knowledge under whose control --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question doesn't reflect the evidence as it is in English just as the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You told us about warehouses that you were fortunate enough to have, and you said fortunate is not perhaps the right word. Can you tell us those warehouses, they belong to whom? What was your answer? What did you say as your first answer to that question, following you are words that "fortunate might not be the right word."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, naturally it is not the right word, since you are talking about victims, about people being killed. It is not civilized to have such things, but it is better to defend yourself than to be dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But my question is: What was then your first answer? You said "fortunately we had warehouses," belonging to whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those warehouses belonged to the Territorial Defence of the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that your first answer right away, or do you now add? Because in your first answer as we read it, was that it belonged to the army, and then Ms. Pilipovic asked you about warehouses belonging to the Territorial Defence, at least, that is what we read in the English transcript. In your first answer, did you mention the Territorial Defence or did you just mention the army? We can check it later, if necessary, but if you know, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Feel free to check it, but these warehouses belonged to the Territorial Defence. That is known, and it is marked on the maps, because in those warehouses, the city of Sarajevo had these warehouses at its disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand what you now tell me. But in you first answer, did you say warehouses belonging to the army, or did you already in your first answer say that they belonged to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those Territorial Defence warehouses. I think I have been clear, and that is clearly marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed. Perhaps we should check during the first break because that gives always the best information, because the witness, of course, is not fully aware perhaps of what the issue is. Please proceed for the time being and perhaps we come back to it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, you told us that you took weapons from the Territorial Defence warehouse in Faletici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other people from your villages in that territory who took weapons from that warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, I know that we armed ourselves by taking weapons from that warehouse because we had been informed that Muslims, our neighbours, also entered that warehouse, they were the first ones to enter the warehouse and to take weapons out. So then we followed and we went to take weapons for ourselves, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To clarify everything, could you tell us with regard to the warehouses that you have mentioned and in which there were weapons, who guarded them and who controlled them before you and members of the Muslim population went there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: During the time of the former Yugoslavia, the Territorial Defence guarded these warehouses. I don't know who was there. I had never entered them before. The first time I entered the warehouses was when we went to take the -- when we went to take the weapons. All I know is that the Territorial Defence was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But within those warehouses, do you know whether the JNA had its premises there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what sort of information there was because at the time I really wasn't familiar with these formations. But I know that it said "TO," Territorial Defence, on the cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, we entered about 1992. I think it was in May or towards the end of April. I can't provide you with the exact dates, with the exact day, but that was the period, roughly speaking. And I have a piece of evidence. It's been proved that they had entered before that because the Zijo Lovcic who had a light machine-gun who had been issued to him, his number was lower than Marko's number. So a Muslim and a Serb had obtained weapons from the same case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, when you say that you entered the warehouse, and I am referring to you in particular, and you said your other members of your nation, when you said that you went to the warehouse, what sort of weapons did you take from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: We took automatic rifles and semi-automatic rifles. We took infantry weapons from the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, you told us that you had organised yourselves and that you armed yourselves. Can you tell us in terms of what sort of formations you made, you composed? I am referring to the inhabitants from the village in which you lived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, we formed the defence for the village at the time when we armed ourselves, we protected village to prevent an escalation from occurring, to prevent rape and slaughter from occurring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. But can you tell us how many of you were there who were military fit who formed that defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, about 70 men formed this defence group. But there were elderly people there too, between 55 and 60 years of age, and even people who were 65 years old. We didn't have enough young people, perhaps, 14 younger men, perhaps 40.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that there were about 70 of you, did you have a particular name, how did you identify yourselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, we did this together and we protected the area together. We were there when the Republika Srpska Army was formed. And later on, we joined as a company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is safe to say that you organised as a company. In that area where the front lines of your company were located, was there a wider military formation that you belonged to? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Later on, we were part of the 7th Battalion; that was after the Army of Republika Srpska had been formed. First they accepted the companies and then a battalion was formed. So then it was one army, just one whole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that area where your company was located, in order to clarify matters, could you tell us where the line of your company was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you that my company's line was from Borije to Moscanica, to the stream, to the Moscanica stream, down there, that's where our line was, called Emerovice and Zecja Glava?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you have told us where the line of your company was, could you tell us, given that you have told us that you belonged to the 4th battalion --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: The Hresanski batallion, the 4th battalion -- I don't know what the name was exactly, because it would change. I think at the beginning it was the 4th battalion and then later, the name changed. So I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge with regard to the number of companies there were in the battalion, let's say that we are speaking about the Hresanski battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: As far as I know, we had five companies in the Hresanski battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, do you have any personal knowledge of the zone of responsibility of the Hresanski battalion, where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well the zone of responsibility of the Hresanski batallion went from Borija and Zecja Glava, where my company was to Donje Bijesko to Barice and as far as Mrkojevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that in your company you were armed with automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether during the period from September 1992 to August 1994, can you tell us whether you had any other weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: No, apart from the fact that we had two mortars, 60-millimetre mortars, which belonged to the company, and that was all the weapons we had. We had the 60-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the period referred to, could you tell us whether there was any fighting in the zone of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: There was fighting on a daily basis on the zone of our company. Almost every day there was fighting there, because they were trying to get in to our villages and we wouldn't allow them to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that there was fighting almost on a daily basis, have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, almost every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, do you personally know, what weapons the BH Army used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: They used all sorts of weapons, rifles, sniper rifles, rocket launchers, even tanks. They fired at the line on two occasions, but they used launchers all the time, and shells fell on our line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, now that you have answered this question, can you tell us what the positions of your company were. From the positions of your company, did you have a view of the so-called urban part of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: You can't see the town very well from my positions. You can see Hadi Brdo where I was, because it was in a sort of gorge, not exactly a gorge, but you couldn't really see it. You could see part of Hadi Brdo and part of Siste so-called shooting site where shooting was practiced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you could see Hadi Brdo, and Siste, the shooting site, yes, can you tell us the positions of Hadi Brdo and Streliste? Whose positions were these? Which army was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: The Muslim army was there. They were at those positions. Hadi Brdo was theirs, it was a Muslim village. The line was in front of that village, and below Donje Bijesko, there was a Serbian line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tell us that you could see positions Hadi Brdo and Streliste from the position of your company, could you tell us how Hresanska and Streliste located with regard to the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, it is a good position because they can see the city. They can see the city from down there, so the position must be good. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to be precise, when you say that the positions were good and that the city could be seen, could you tell us which part of the city was closest to Hladivode and Streliste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, Sedrenik, the upper part of village towards Sedrenik, that was the part closest to Stelici. And Hladivode is closer to Vasan Han and to those areas there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, with regard to your company, can you -- and with regard to the battalion, can you tell us who the commander of the battalion in Hresa was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, this wasn't a secret. Milan Pakalovic was the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about whether he was a professional military man or was he an inhabitant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: He was from Donje Bijesko. He wasn't a professional military man. He had some influence and he reached a certain position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to your company, can you tell us were there any professional soldiers in your company, and when I say "professional soldiers," I am referring to members of the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: No, we didn't have such men. We were inhabitants from those villages, and we didn't have any professional men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any such men in the battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: No, I don't know about the battalion. There weren't any such men in the battalion as far as I know. But to tell you the truth, I never asked who was an active duty member and who wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP21, do you know where the command post was, the Hresa battalion command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, it was in Hresa in Misinovic's house, that's where the command post was located. And the people from the surrounding villages, we moved them out, we moved them away from the line in case of a breakthrough. We wanted to make sure that the people would not be killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you moved the people away from the line, could you be a little bit specific? Where did you move them away from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, let's say behind the line, all the people who lived behind the line, we would send up to Hresa, to the centre where there was no shelling, there was no shooting. So the woman and children, we would send them up there. Sometimes someone would come to visit their relatives, but we moved certain people away. Tadic, we moved this person away, et cetera --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Don't mention too many names. When you say you "moved them away," can you tell us who inhabited in those houses, the houses from which people had been moved away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, Serbs, they were there. We moved them away because of the action. Because when the shelling started, when the Muslims started shelling, then shells started falling on their houses --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, I think you have answered that question. I wanted you to tell us whether those houses from which people had been moved out, did anyone use those houses while the conflict was raging?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, no one used them because they couldn't be used. It was dangerous to live there, so the army didn't allow anyone to live there. Sometimes when they said there would be a strike, we would be in those houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, in the area of your company and of your battalion too, from September 1992 until August 1994, can you tell us whether any buildings had been damaged, any buildings that were in the area of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Do you mean behind the line?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean in general in the area of your company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, yes, there was damage. For example, when there was an exchange of fire, when the Muslims started firing on us, for example, a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. bullet would hit a house, sometimes a shell would fly over us, and it would explode in the village. Around those houses, behind us, the damage wasn't extensive, but there was damage to facades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, I think that you have told us that with regard to the zone of your company, the Muslims fired from tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, they did fire from Streliste. I saw them with my own eyes. They fired two shells in the direction of my line. I saw that with my own eyes. That was about 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, when you spoke about your company, you mentioned the weapons, the positions, and the length of the line of your company; but can you tell us: Were the members of your company, did they have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: No, we didn't have uniforms. Some people were wearing civilian clothes. Some people were in the reserve police force and they would wear their uniforms, but mostly the members of the company wore civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict, can you tell us whether you as a member of the company that you called Hresanska company, can you tell us whether your company had a different name later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: No, it was also called the Hresanska company of the Hresanska battalion. It didn't have any other name; that was the only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you as a member of the Hresanska company received orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, we received orders from our command, that is to say from the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what sort of orders did you receive from the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, we received orders not to fire. We were ordered only to return fire when they started firing at us. If they advanced on us, we were told to defend ourselves, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how often such orders were issued?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, occasionally because quite often men would be killed or wounded, then new men would arrive. And we received those orders, but we also had a permanent order, according to which we had to respect the Geneva Conventions. And we were told that we shouldn't fire on civilians and we were told how to behave if we captured people, although this never happened, but often we were given these orders verbally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You as a member of the Hresanska company, could you tell us, when these orders were issued, where were they issued?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, they were issued over the phone or verbally at the line, directly at the line. We would be ordered not to do this or that, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "verbally" or "over the phone," what did you want to tell us with regard to the telephone? Could you clarify the issue of the telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, there was a line between us and the command. For example, there was a telephone in the command; it would ring. And then they would be told what the situation was, if someone was shot they would be told why there was shooting. No one could shoot whenever they wanted to shoot, so there was certain control and it was necessary to save ammunition and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, you told us that you also had two mortars in your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said 60-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use those mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, yes, we did. We defended ourselves with those mortars. When our line was attacked, then naturally, the mortars would be used in order to defend ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often were these so-called defensive attacks, how often did they take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, sometimes these defensive attacks would take place every day, sometimes every other day. There was shooting all the time. There were attacks all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, with regard to your company's line, and let's say the line of your battalion too, what sort of lines of communication did you have to the command? What brigade was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, I think it was the 1st Romanija brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the command post of your brigade was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: No, I don't know, because it wasn't necessary for me to know this. I never went there. I was mostly on the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to your villages and other villages too, could you tell us whether there was a road there, a route there that was important for you as inhabitants of those villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: I don't know which road. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To be more specific, how could you communicate during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, we came from Hresa towards Sarajevo to Zecja Glava, if that's what you mean to say. If you want to say which road we -- which route we used to defend that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you linked up to other municipalities and were there any links?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, we had links to Sokolac municipality and Sumbalac [phoen] and we were linked to Pale through Sumbalac [phoen]. That was -- our rear was a free zone, there was no shooting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, when you told us that your buildings at the front line had been damaged, could you be more specific and tell us what caused the damage to these buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: The damage was caused by bullets and by shells fired at us because they probably weren't very precise when they fired. There were houses behind us, and they would be hit by shells and damage would be inflicted, naturally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, you told us that you dug trenches at your line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally know how front lines of the BH Army were formed with regard to the line of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, the BH Army lines, I don't know how they were formed. But they were in front of us and they formed a line. They probably had offices there. I don't know how it worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the front lines of the BH Army, do you know whether there were trenches there too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, there were trenches. They would dig trenches in front of us and interconnecting trenches, just as we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to the front line of your company, can you tell us how far the demarcation line was between you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, 150 metres as the crow flies, at some places, and other places, 2 to 300 metres as the crow flies. Because it depended on the layout of the terrain. It wasn't regular.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me just confer with my co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my co-counsel will ask a few questions and then we would finish our examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The questions that I wish to ask you are the following: When the shells landed you spoke to us about these shells that landed, did they leave any traces on the soil, and if yes, which ones? What were they like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: These shells did leave traces on the soil where they would become activated. They would leave craters. There would be soil dispersed if Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. they would fall on the soil. But, of course, if they would fall on the asphalt, then there wouldn't be so much damage, because it couldn't inflict such damage, it couldn't disperse so much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke to us about asphalt areas. Could you tell us what are the diametres of the shells that were used against you, if you know, as far as you know, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, according to the remains that were fired on them, so a tail-fin would be left. The body -- the body of a shell has a tail-fin which directed -- I don't quite know what the right term is. But it's like a mortar which propels it. A mortar that propels it. So this was like 82 millimetre, 60 millimetres, so these were three different types of mortar shells that were fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe, again, that I heard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The French transcript which, if I am not mistaken, mentioned 120 millimetres as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only that, but particularly in Serbian, what the witness said, he spoke of the 120 millimetres as the weapons, and it is not in the transcript, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask the French translators whether I did understand you well whether you mentioned 120? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned to start with a 120-millimetre shell, and could you tell us whether you were able to observe, yes or no, crater traces of 120-millimetre shells in the area that you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw craters in the area. I saw that on many occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you saw these craters of 120-millimetre shells on the asphalt, I am speaking only about the asphalt craters, would you be able to describe them to the Chamber? Could you tell us, what did they look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, yes, I could. The shell would hit in a spot and a part of the asphalt would be damaged and then there would be some kind of a hole, about 55 centimetres. If it was a bigger shell, if it was 82, then it would be slightly smaller, then 60 would be even smaller because the charge would be lighter, so the crater wouldn't be so great.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you speak of a hole, could you describe this hole. What did it look like? Is it deep? It is a shallow hole? What can you tell us about it, according to what you have seen about the craters of 120-millimetre calibre shells?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: 120-millimetre shells on the asphalt, it would be a hard terrain, so the depth would be 20, 25 centimetres, and of course, on a meadow it would be deeper, of course, because more soil would be lifted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in these 120-millimetre calibre shells, shell attacks, when they hit what's left is the tail-fin that you have described. According to your experience, where did they land?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, not only to leading, but as it transpired of making a statement and moving on to a question on this issue which is not included in our 65 ter summary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first question is not leading, because what I am asking, where is the tail-fin going to end up, which is not leading. Now, if you read our letter of the 29th, it says that we will speak about the weapons, how they were used, and I believe that all the questions in relation to the weapons are admissible. We cannot be more precise than what we have already been precise, so that we can defend General Galic, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first part of the objection is denied. The second part, whether this should have been in the summary, the Chamber will discuss this in due course and give further guidance on that issue. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, according to your experience of combat, fighting, that you had, what could you tell the Chamber about what happened as a general rule with 120-millimetre tail-fin when the shell hit a part of an asphalt area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: It would fall off and it would jump off some 2 or 3 metres away from the crater, it will probably be found. And that is also a good way to find out what kind of shell -- what the calibre was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it in your professional experience that you have had on the front line, is it how it always happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, it always happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, now I'd like you to ask you another question. Have you ever heard of the existence of a plan of your that would have been structured in such a way to have the objective to eradicate, eliminate, all Muslim population of Sarajevo, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I think I should start asking you whether you are ready to start cross-examining the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I am not. One of the difficulties that I have is that the 65 ter summary indicated that the witness would indicate the positions of which he would give evidence on a map, and indeed the Defence, as I've indicated, has told us that they intended to use the map. And thus having elicited from the witness names of a number of places, the Defence then sits down not having required the witness to mark the map. Mr. President, in my respectful submission, that should be done by the Defence so that the Prosecution can better be informed of what the evidence is and then respond. Mr. President, if you do not require the Defence to do that in their time, then I will need an adjournment so I can make the relevant enquiries as to precisely where a number of the places are that the witness has mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we thought it was useful in order to preserve everyone's means, we thought it would be a good idea to proceed in this way. We had a meeting with the victims and witness unit in order to preserve the chronology indicated. We thought that in order to avoid a waste of time because we all have -- we all know how to read a map, and the witness told us about names, locations, told us about a stream. It would be easier to find the names, the location on the map. If we are asked to waste time, we will do it. But, of course, otherwise, the witness just has to stay longer in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence prepared the map, and I also gave it to -- also gave it to the case manager. It is P3274. But considering the second witness who is on the same line, so the Defence didn't want to take double time to do two maps for the same front line. If the Chamber believes it is useful, we will ask the witness to look at the map and we can resolve that problem, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered the matter. Ms. Pilipovic, the Chamber would also, for its own orientation, very much appreciate if you would show the map to the witness. And the Chamber is, of course -- fully agrees that it is of no use to present repetitious evidence in this respect. But if there are two witnesses, and if one of them will indicate the front line positions, then it is more comfortable, at least for us, to hear it from the first witness so that we don't have to guess too much. So if you would please introduce that map. And as said, we are not asking for repetitious evidence, we are just asking to do Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it now rather than in the near future.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I just like number --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise. But General Galic tells me that the second witness is a professional soldier, and that he would be a lot more at ease with the maps. We will do this now with the map, but this does not mean that we will renounce to use the map with the second witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not saying that. Let's just see where we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And also, Your Honour, if the Registry could give me the following number. Is it 1788? Is it D1788 or should we just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't imagine, Ms. Pilipovic, that you do not in too much detail, but at least we have a global orientation of where we are. Perhaps leave the details for the professional.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, on your right-hand side there is a map or a part of a map. I would just like to ask you not to mark this in. If you can just indicate locations with the pointer please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: I will show you the location where this Hresa company was in front of Zecja Glava. I will show it to you here. Well, I can see this -- a lot more is even on the screen. Here you have Emerovice, and here this is a high power line which went here. These were the pylons and somewhere here -- somewhere here was my line. Two, there is the stream and from that where the stream is, it would go all the way to Borija. That is where my company held. Now, the other lines I wouldn't be able to show you properly because I am not fully trained for this and I didn't go and look at the lines. But I know that this line up to here, above Emerovice and there is Hresa here. You can see exactly that is where I was on the line. And you have here some houses. This is Topalovic and again you see the Tadic houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, could you please take a black fine liner and mark on the map the area of responsibility of your company, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Can I have the black pen, please. Can I use this one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we use different colours for the parties who is asking you to mark. So it should be the one given to you by the -- it should be a black one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I respect that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I just thought that it would be easier, but you can give me whichever colour you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then use a black ballpoint for the time being and certainly we will ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, as the area of responsibility of your company, you've marked the positions above the village called Emerovice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Emerovice, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have marked the positions of your company. Could you mark the positions of the BH Army in relation to yours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, I can. From what I have seen, it is approximately here. I will do it with a dotted line like this, like this, and here there is an elevation point. It is an elevation. It could be about here. So it is from there that they use sniper fire very often. So this was the line in front of us, that was located there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, can you tell us what was the length of the front line of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: I really didn't measure. I don't know exactly what the length was, but I know that it was in this area, perhaps a kilometre and a half, approximately. It is probably not more than that. That is 1.500 metres from there. You can see this part we covered, as much as I am able to see. And here there is the stream, so it would go up to the stream. This road here was not under our control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us about Zecja Glava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see it on the map here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, Novi Rad [phoen], Emerovice, it doesn't say here, but Zecja Glava is here, its houses are here. If you want me to indicate them, I can mark them. These are the houses here on Zecja Glava; that's what it is. These are the locations. We call it Zecja Glava, but it is really not written as much on the map. Emerovice was below, and then near Vasin Han was the Barabana [phoen], so these are the directions. And above Zecja Glava and Gromova [phoen] above from the left above is Faletici and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, this line, this communication line that goes below Amerivica, Aluge, and Bronobay [phoen], can you tell us, what is this marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: These are meadows. These are fields. And this is the road which goes above. This is the main road and below it you have meadows in Aluge and Bronobay [phoen] Oru Movi. These are meadows, grazing fields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say main road which one is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: This is the main road leading to Hersa that Aluge and Bronobai. You can this is Hresa, and here you can see 1.150 metres, and it goes to Zemunica. So that was what we had with the Sokalac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP21, thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: You are welcome

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This would be a suitable time then for the break. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is the Prosecution ready to start to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, would you then please escort the witness into the courtroom. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, very briefly, and in a couple of words, since you were to provide some information with regard to 65 ter, I would like to draw your attention to the fact that in November 2002, very not long ago, we mentioned a lot of details about the tanks of the enemy, the means used, the mortars, et cetera, et cetera, and we provided Mr. Ierace with this information. So we tried to specify all of these items. There were also elements that we decided not to mention simply to save time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...in more detail. Mr. DP21, you will now be further examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you the commander of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, I was the commander of my company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us earlier this morning about your observations of tail-fins and craters created by mortars fired at you of the calibre of 120 millimetres. How often were such mortars fired at you, that is, 120 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, you can't assess that it's just 120-millimetre shells, because if you go and check to see what the calibre is, someone could die. They shelled very soften. Sometimes the shells were 120-millimetre shells sometimes 82-millimetre shells and sometimes 60-millimetre shells. If you have a look to see where a shell fell, if you analyse how well it was directed or not, well, then you could see that. But I didn't go to examine this every time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that it is difficult to say how many of these craters were created by 120-millimetre shells as opposed to 82-millimetre shells or 60-millimetre shells? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes. There was a lot of shooting, a lot of shelling. They shelled on several occasions, on many occasions. I didn't count the number of occasions. I wasn't interested in that. I was interested in getting out, saving my life, and the lives of the inhabitants who were on the line, and I was interested in taking shelter, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us this morning that your company obtained automatic and semi-automatic rifles from the warehouse at Faletici. When did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: We didn't receive that, but as civilians in the local commune, we had a meeting just before the war broke out, so to speak, that is to say on the 2nd of April. And we would tear our hair out wondering what to do. We were endangered, and as I had worked in the village for 20 years --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. The general rule is to let the witness continue when he is speaking about matters that could be of interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just reread the question and -- yes, you gave a lot of information. But the question was: When did you obtain automatic and semi-automatic rifles from the warehouse in Faletici? So at what time? Please proceed. Or could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer the question. That was in May. We went spontaneously as the inhabitants of the Hresa local commune. These were people who were defending their village. They went to take a rifle and return to their positions because we thought it was going to be dangerous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to give you some guidance, whether you did it spontaneously or whether it was dangerous or not, if Mr. Ierace is interested to hear that, he will certainly ask you. He first asked you when and your answered that question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the warehouse, was anyone guarding it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: There were no guards at the warehouse. There were a net of sort of protective fence but it had broken down and you could get through and enter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that the opposing forces had been there before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, I know that because of the piece of evidence that I mentioned this morning, the Zijo Lovcic had a machine-gun and a number of which was lower than that of Marko Cavarkapa. The numbers of from 1 to 10, 10 to 20 and the number of the weapons in the cases. So both weapons were taken from the same case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that because a combatant on the other side had a machine-gun with a particular number, you were able to deduce that it came from Faletici and that it had been obtained from there earlier than yours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you that it is not believable that the opposing forces, if they had gone to the warehouse first, would have taken arms and left other arms behind for your forces to come and collect them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: I say that they entered just like we did. We didn't take all the weapons, but everyone took a few weapons, two or three weapons. They did the same, perhaps. Because it is one people, you could say, in terms of their ideas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I further suggest to you that what in fact happened was as the time of hostilities approached, the JNA moved the contents of the warehouse to ensure that Bosniak forces could not obtain them. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, they didn't transfer them. They left a lot of weapons for the Bosniak people, such as the Marshal Tito Barracks or the command in Bistrik, the headquarters of the JNA, and for example, the Viktor Bubanj place. All the weapons remained down there because if they hadn't remained there, where would they have obtained weapons from? They weren't in a position to produce them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the ABiH control part of the Faletici area until about July 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, in front of the gate, the BH Army held that part, and naturally the conditions were more favourable for them to enter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You drew on a map the part of the confrontation line that the company you commanded held. What was the name of the company that held the line immediately north of your section?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: North of our section, the name of the company was -- are you referring to the Serbian positions? I haven't understood you. They were -- I apologize. Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the Serbian company, the Serbian part of the -- the Bosnian Serbian part of the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: The name of the Serbian company was Bijustanska company. Because above them was Donje Bijesko, and these people were people from those villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only weaponry other than rifles that you have mentioned that the Bosnian Serb forces had in your area were two 60-millimetre mortars. Was there artillery in the area of Hresa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: It was in the Hresa area, the artillery was there, that is to say in the Borije area, that's the name. I don't know what the name is exactly, but there was artillery in Borije.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far is that from Hresa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Borije is about 2 and a half kilometers from Hresa. I can't tell you what the exact distance, but I think that that's the distance. I didn't measure it, so I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that artillery give you support from time to time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes, they did give us support when dangerous attacks were launched against us, because the Muslim formation was far stronger than the formation in which I was. So this is why we had to ask for artillery support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also have support in the form of 120-millimetre mortars from areas outside your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, the artillery did its job up there. They made their own assessments, whether they needed to use 120-millimetre shells, et cetera. But I am not informed about that. But there was artillery support, but I don't know exactly what they used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they used artillery or large-calibre mortars, did your company fulfill the function of observers for them to ensure accuracy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: We couldn't carry out reconnaissance to see what they were firing from because we were in a lower position with regard to the Muslims who were in Orlovac above us. So it wasn't possible for us to leave the trenches, the dugouts, because we would have been hit and we would had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is there any need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to confer with my colleague. Perhaps there is one issue. Yes, just one matter. Re-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, at line 38.8 you mentioned the fact that the BH Army was more or less at the gates, that is how you put it. I am talking about Faletici. How were you able to get into those warehouses if the enemy was present? What can you tell us about this incursion that you carried out, about this entry into the premises of the Territorial Defence. That is my first question; there will be a second one afterwards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, they were at the entrance, at the gate of the Territorial Defence warehouse. We were on the other side. We entered through the fence that had been broken down because the diametre was about a kilometre and a half. So we entered from the opposite side. We got in and naturally we hid to make sure that they wouldn't hit us, and then we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. took what we needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was fire opened at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: No. When we were leaving, fire was opened, but then it subsided. We got out, there weren't any wounded people, no one was killed, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, a minute ago you were asked about the alleged transfer of former JNA weapons, and you said that the cases had the inscription TO, that is to say, Territorial Defence. And my question is as follows: Did all the cases of weapons that you saw bear this inscription, the TO inscription on them?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps my learned colleague --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- could refer me to the line where that was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The TO, inscription, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, has been mentioned. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can do so, but I think the witness stated this very clearly, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have the line available, it certainly would assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have it available, but I will have a look for it. We will find it under Defence, I think. It is on page 14, Mr. President. It is the line 14 in my transcript [In English] Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, in that case, it is a matter which arose in examination-in-chief, not in cross-examination, as to the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, not exactly, Mr. President. During the cross-examination Mr. Ierace mentioned the hypothesis, according to which the army allegedly transferred everything from the warehouse to prevent it from falling into Muslim hands, the hands of the Muslim forces. This is a new issue. And what I wanted to know, is in all of these cases, since the witness mentioned them, naturally during the cross-examination, but given Mr. Ierace's question, I wanted to know whether all these cases bore the inscription TO, Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer of the witness where he says that there were cases where a TO inscription, that was not specifically sought by the question. It was a spontaneous extra to what the question was to the witness. Mr. Ierace, you paid specific attention especially to obtaining weapons and, therefore, the Defence is allowed to ask specific questions -- to go in more detail where it did not specifically seek this information in an earlier stage, but in a very global scale. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would appreciate it if you could answer the question that I have just put to you. To the best of your knowledge, when you entered these warehouses, with regard to the weapons, the cases of weapons and the TO inscription that you mentioned, that is to say the Territorial Defence inscription, did all the cases that you saw in the warehouse bear this inscription?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, the ones that I saw, the cases that I saw, did have these inscriptions. TO was inscribed on all of them. There were numbers there and there was a big case, perhaps 130 centimetres long and 40 centimetres wide. And on the cover, on the lid it said "TO," and on the side of the cases you could also see the TO inscription.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi has one or more questions to you. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] I would like you to tell me, please, whether you know when you started digging the trenches, and if you do know, when did the enemy start digging their own trenches? Can you remember who started? Did you start? Did the enemy start? Do you know the date, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: We started digging trenches towards the end of 1992 and 1993, and in 1993 we were mostly in trenches and we were prepared. As soon as the artillery shooting a bit, that was in 1992, there was some loud explosion that was behind me, near Mocra Moguste [phoen]. These shells started falling, and we automatically began to dig in because we were in danger of being killed. After that, they started digging in front of our -- below our positions, and that's how both sides formed trenches. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. And if I have understood you correctly, it was around the end of 1992 and at the beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. And my second question, if possible: Could you tell me how you could distinguish mortar shell calibres? Was it easy for you, your company was composed of volunteers, people who weren't professionals, was it easy for you to distinguish between 60-millimetre, 82-millimetre, and 120-millimetre calibre. What could you tell us with regard to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well, I could tell you at the beginning it was difficult to distinguish it calibres, because we didn't understand this. But with experience and as the war advanced, I could tell the difference between 60-millimetre, 82-millimetre, and 120-millimetre shells. I could even recognise a tank shell, because the misfortune that we experienced taught us about these matters. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. But in your company you only had 60-millimetre mortars, so you didn't have 120-millimetre mortars yourselves? You hadn't seen 120-millimetre shell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: No I hadn't seen a 120-millimetre shell because we didn't have such shells. We had two 60-millimetre mortars, and the man who helped us, he wasn't very qualified in that area. This is just something to use to help ourselves because we didn't have 120-millimetre shells. We didn't have such mortars. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. So with regard to the two 60-millimetre mortars that you had, you said that you and professionals and the men, individuals, who used these mortars, could they distinguish targets, distinguish -- could they recognise the zone that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. they wanted to attack? Could they recognise targets? How did they act, how did they proceed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: Well they carried out that task. We knew where the enemy line was, and they would assess the distance between the lines, roughly, and that's how we would defend ourselves. You could see for 150 metres, 200 metres with the naked eye, you could see the line where they had dug in, you could see the land where they had dug out, and that's where the shell would fall. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, because you said that the enemy side was in an -- was on elevated terrain. So was it possible to see them from your positions? Was there a view from your positions? And did you only attack the trenches that you could see or did you attack the rear of the enemy side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: We never attacked anyone. We were just defending ourselves from evil. We didn't even see any civilians because they were behind. You couldn't see behind the hill. You could see where the line was and this is where we were. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] But, your mortars, the ones that you had, where did your mortar shells fall? Was it necessarily on the lines or sometimes -- did they sometimes fall behind the lines? Because you changed the positions of the mortars, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: We didn't change the positions of the mortars. They remained at their positions, and they were used very seldom. Only when intense attacks were launched, in order to repel the enemy attack, we would use the mortars. If the infantry couldn't resist the attacks since the attacks were of very large scale and we were afraid because there weren't enough of us for that formation. They had very strong formations, very strong units, as you can see now. This was shown on the television. At the time, we didn't know. But on the basis of the fire they used, we were able to see that they had many men, many soldiers, many Muslim soldiers. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Well, my very last question, please, is in relation to the damage that you were able to see for yourself, damage done by shells that came from the enemy side on your positions. Was the soil, was it asphalt? Was it soil? Was it hard soil? What type of soil was it where the shells landed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP21
utterances.text: There were several types of terrain. There was the asphalt road in which the shells landed. Then there were fields. And there was also a part of the grazing meadow where also shells landed. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
